events.title: Washington Creates the Badge of Military Merit
events.description: At his headquarters in Newburgh, New York, General George Washington announced the Badge of Military Merit. It was a purple heart-shaped award for soldiers who showed extraordinary merit in the Continental Army.
events.significance: The badge is regarded as the forerunner of the Purple Heart. Today that medal honors U.S. service members who are wounded or killed in action.

events.title: U.S. Marines Land on Guadalcanal
events.description: About 6,000 American Marines came ashore on Guadalcanal and nearby islands in the Solomons. They quickly seized a nearly finished Japanese airfield at Lunga Point.
events.significance: This was the first major Allied land offensive against Japan in the Pacific. It began a grueling six-month campaign that helped turn the tide of the war.

events.title: Congress Passes the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution
events.description: After reports of attacks on U.S. Navy ships off the coast of Vietnam, Congress approved a resolution giving President Lyndon B. Johnson broad authority to use military force in Southeast Asia. It did not include a formal declaration of war.
events.significance: The resolution became the legal basis for the major escalation of U.S. involvement in the Vietnam War. It also fueled long-running debate over the limits of presidential war powers.

events.title: U.S. Embassies Bombed in East Africa
events.description: Nearly simultaneous truck bombs exploded outside the American embassies in Nairobi, Kenya, and Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. The attacks were carried out by Osama bin Laden's al-Qaeda network.
events.significance: The attacks killed hundreds of people, most of them Africans, and brought al-Qaeda to global attention. They were a grim warning of the larger attacks that followed on September 11, 2001.
